scenarios.desc: Oversized, branchy method with an explanatory comment
scenarios.input: src/Orders/OrderService.cs has ProcessOrder at about 85 lines with cyclomatic complexity around 14, and one block carries a long comment explaining what it does. I want to clean it up. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Style and Structure: methods stay under 60 lines and keep cyclomatic complexity at or below 10, and the rule says to extract a private method before writing a comment that explains a block.

scenarios.desc: Large struct passed by value in a hot loop
scenarios.input: In src/Geometry/Vector4D.cs the readonly struct holds four doubles (32 bytes) and is passed by value to Dot and Cross inside a tight loop. Profiling shows extra copying. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Allocation and Performance: pass large structs by in to avoid defensive copies, and a struct over about 16 bytes passed by value is usually a mistake. Measure with BenchmarkDotNet before and after.

scenarios.desc: Library async method that ignores token and ConfigureAwait
scenarios.input: src/Parsing/CsvReader.cs is a class library. ReadRowsAsync awaits a stream read, has no CancellationToken parameter, and a sync wrapper calls .Result on it. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Async section: an awaitable crossing an I/O boundary takes and honors a CancellationToken, libraries use ConfigureAwait(false) on every await, and .Result or .Wait() is never used to block. The caller must become async.

scenarios.desc: New xUnit test file with over-mocking and loose names
scenarios.input: I am creating tests/Orders/OrderServiceTests.cs. I plan to mock OrderService itself with Moq to verify calls and name tests Test1 and Test2. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
expected_signals: do not mock the type under test
scenarios.rationale: Tooling section: mocks go at boundaries only and never on the type under test, and tests are named Method_State_ExpectedOutcome.

scenarios.desc: Same async concerns in a TypeScript file (negative)
scenarios.input: In src/api/orders.ts the fetchOrders function is 90 lines and awaits several calls without an AbortSignal. Suggest how to restructure it. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The rule's paths cover .cs, .csproj, Directory.Build.*, .cshtml, and .razor. A TypeScript file is adjacent in concern but out of scope, so C# limits and CancellationToken guidance do not apply.

scenarios.input: Add a Logging:LogLevel override for Microsoft.AspNetCore to src/Api/appsettings.Development.json. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: appsettings.Development.json matches none of the rule's globs, so the C# idiom rules do not activate for a plain JSON settings edit.
